reasoning: A legal system is conventionally described as comprising the basic values and principles of the Constitution, the substantive rights and obligations created by ordinary statutes, the organisational machinery that enforces them within constitutional limits, and the persons on whom legal personality is conferred. All four statements name a part of that whole, so the inclusive option is correct.
basis: Both passes rated this MED and agreed on statements 1-3, splitting only on statement 4 — pass A including it, pass B arguing that legal persons are SUBJECTS of a legal system rather than components of it. Adjudicated to A because statement 4 answers the stem under BOTH readings of its ambiguous wording: the page prints 'legal and JUDICIAL persons', and if that is read literally (judges and judicial officers) they are plainly part of the system's machinery, while if it is a misprint for the standard term 'juristic persons' those are the legal entities the system constitutes and recognises. A statement that qualifies either way cannot be the one the setter meant to exclude. Note also that pass B's own reasoning silently substituted 'juristic' for the printed 'judicial'. No official key exists for this paper.
